name: Sulawesi Honey-buzzard
rangeDescription: Sulawesi region, including togian, banggai, and sula islands (off eastern sulawesi) and muna and buton (to southeast)
description: A small-headed, long-tailed raptor from Sulawesi and the Banggai Islands. Adult shows a dark crested head, a pale throat with dark central stripe, a rufous breast with bold streaking, and a barred belly.

name: Palawan Babbler
rangeDescription: Southwestern philippines (balabac and palawan)
description: A medium-sized bird of lowland forest tangles and bamboo on Palawan and Balabac. Medium-brown above with more rufous on the tail, shoulder, and forecrown.

name: Black Solitaire
rangeDescription: West slope of western andes of colombia (chocó) and northwestern ecuador
description: This striking thrush is unmistakable if seen well: mostly jet black with a white cheek, white tuft under the shoulder, and white outer tail feathers (easily visible from below). Also note red eye and orange lower mandible.

name: Crescent-faced Antpitta
rangeDescription: Locally in andes of southern colombia and ecuador
description: Small, striking antpitta that lurks in bamboo-laden cloud forest at very high elevations in the Andes. Brown and gray with white crescents on face, streaked underparts, and buffy spots on sides of neck.

name: Buckley's Forest-Falcon
rangeDescription: Humid amazon forest of eastern ecuador and eastern peru
description: Elusive falcon of lowland and foothill rainforest east of the Andes. Note black upperparts, white underparts, white hindcollar, and dull yellow face.

name: Blackish Chat-Tyrant
rangeDescription: Andes of western venezuela (mérida, western barinas, and táchira)
description: Small flycatcher endemic to the Venezuela Andes. Plumage is entirely slate gray except for its conspicuous white eyebrows, which can shine like headlights in the gloom.
imageCreditName: Jhonathan Miranda - Wandering Venezuela Birding Expeditions

name: Rouget's Rail
rangeDescription: Highlands of eritrea and ethiopia
description: This unusual rail can be quite tame, and is often found well away from water. The upperparts are olive-brown, the underparts are rufous, and the bright white undertail is often revealed when the tail is flicked up while walking.

name: Yellow-throated Leafbird
rangeDescription: Southwestern philippines (balabac, busuanga, palawan, and calamian)
description: A medium-sized bird of lowland forest canopy and edge on Palawan and neighboring islands. Joins mixed-species flocks, often with bulbuls, foraging for fruits and seeds.

name: White-throated Daggerbill
rangeDescription: Both slopes of western andes and west slope of central andes of colombia and west slope of andes of western ecuador
description: Fairly small hummingbird found on the west slope of the Andes from central Colombia to southwestern Ecuador. Both sexes mostly green with short, straight bill.

name: Southern Ground-Hornbill
rangeDescription: Savanna of eastern and southern africa
description: This enormous, sociable, ground-loving hornbill is easily recognized. The adult male has an extensive brilliant red face and throat wattles, while the adult female has purple-blue skin in the center of the red throat patch.

name: Malabar Flameback
rangeDescription: Western ghats and coastal western india
description: A large, crested woodpecker with a golden-olive back endemic to wet lowland and foothill forests in southwestern India. Separated from Common Flameback and other “small-billed” flamebacks by a much larger bill, a mottled black-and-white nape instead of a black nape, and a divided black horizontal stripe below the cheek.

name: Jet Antbird
rangeDescription: Eastern panama (including pearl islands) to western ecuador and eastern venezuela
description: Small slender antbird, found in pairs skulking through low tangles in forest and edges. Male is very dark black with obvious white fringes on shoulder.

name: Patagonian Forest Earthcreeper
rangeDescription: Central chile and southwestern argentina
description: Rather local breeder in drier Patagonian areas with open forest and shrubby slopes. Migrates across the Andes to winter in Chile, where it is found in matorral and other shrubby habitats.

name: Orange Minivet
rangeDescription: Western peninsular india (southeastern gujarat southward through the western ghats, and southwestern eastern ghats in tamil nadu), and sri lanka
description: Brightly-colored forest bird with a long tail. Male is decked out in black and orange-red, female in gray and yellow.

name: Santa Marta Bush-Tyrant
rangeDescription: Santa marta mountains (northeastern colombia)
description: Scarce flycatcher found only at higher elevations in Colombia’s Santa Marta Mountains. Quite similar to the more widespread Streak-throated Bush-Tyrant, but can be distinguished by the indistinct and less extensive streaking on the throat and lack of cinnamon at the base of the underside of the tail; whistled calls are shorter, clearer, and descend more in pitch.

name: Peruvian Piedtail
rangeDescription: Subtropical southeastern peru (huánuco, pasco, puno, and cusco)
description: Small hummingbird found in montane forest, especially on outlying ridges of the Andes. Green above with orange sides and a white belly that extends onto the sides of its neck; it gets its name from its bold black-and-white striped tail pattern, which is especially visible in flight.

name: Togian White-eye
rangeDescription: Togian islands (off sulawesi)
description: A small green songbird with a black forehead, a yellow throat, and white underparts except for the base of the undertail, which is also yellow. Note the indistinct, intermittent white eye-ring.

name: Cocos Finch
rangeDescription: Forest of cocos island (off western costa rica)
description: Plump, short-tailed bird found only on Cocos Island, located in the Pacific Ocean about 300 miles southwest of mainland Costa Rica. Sexes look quite different.

name: Black-headed Hemispingus
rangeDescription: Andes of colombia to southwestern venezuela and far northern peru
description: A unique little songbird found in the temperate zone of the Andes from extreme western Venezuela to northern Peru. Not bright, but distinctively patterned with a black head, a buffy central crown stripe, staring pale eyes, and a gray body.

name: Citril Finch
rangeDescription: Montane coniferous forest of southern europe
description: Small alpine finch with a quite long pointed bill and long tail. Males have a yellow-green body with gray crown and neck.
